note: Widgets awaiting an audit, with the reason each is in the queue. The practitioner opened this on 2026-10-14 while auditing the decision-producing widgets: "Those widgets need auditing too. Let's put them all in our audit bin." A queue is only useful if it can be seen shrinking, so `pendingCeiling` may be lowered and never raised, and a widget leaves only by having an audit record that names it. Entries are findings, not verdicts: being in the queue says nobody has looked, not that anything is wrong.
ceilingRule: pendingCeiling may be lowered freely and never raised. Removing an entry requires `auditedIn` naming a document that exists and mentions the node type; scripts/validate-audit-queue.mjs enforces both.
